invbst.reason: Too close by the screen: all four seeds 0.64-0.67 (the threshold is 0.45). The side by side is clearly ours (an upright dark oak pole with smooth riveted caps and a leather grip, against the original's slanted pale banded staff with studded ends), and the cross check says it is the shape class: this original scores 0.45 or more against 45 of 60 candidates of the other long pictures, the gnarled staff and the winged Horadric staff among them. The cause: a rod has no interior 2 px in, so similarity.py's edge_in falls back to the outline F1 and outline overlap carries 0.40 of the score, and two rods of the same width and length overlap. A probe (scratch: our s202 cut-out stretched sideways with PIL, not a picture) drops it with thickness: x1.0 0.67, x1.4 0.51, x1.8 0.49, x2.4 0.40.

fix.desc: A battle staff, a war mage's heavy fighting staff: a long, straight, stout pole of mid-brown seasoned oak, thick and heavy, about a tenth as thick as it is long; its middle third wrapped in a broad hand grip of wound dark leather cord, a little wider than the pole, between two flared iron collars; each end shod with a short, plain, blunt iron cap a little wider than the pole, no studs and no spikes, no bands along the bare wood. A thick heavy staff, far stouter than a walking staff. Shown perfectly upright, one iron-capped end at the top.

fix.note: the thickness is the fix: about twice run-04's, a 1x rod of ~13 px in the 34 px cell (run-04's are 6-8 px); keep it a staff, not a club (no swelling head). The iron-shod ends stay, they are the line's part; plain caps, not the original's studs

invhst.reason: The head came out a bat: all four seeds put a beast's head with ears and a snout on the medallion and spread membrane bat wings behind it, so the order's holy staff reads as a demon's at 34 px (the words asked for two metal wings round a medallion, nothing else); s404 is also over the line (0.479, its wings the widest).

fix.desc: The completed staff of an ancient order of mages: the same shaft as its headless shaft's words (invmsf): a straight rod of dark bronze with a thick carved serpent of worn brass coiling round it from foot to top in five open turns, its head resting just under the top; crowned with a head of tarnished bronze: a round medallion set with a small milky white stone, sitting straight on the shaft's socket, and from either side of it a stylised wing of four long flat bronze feather-plates, each a plain leaf-shaped blade, fanned upward and outward in a narrow V, their tips no higher than a hand above the medallion; the wings are plain metal ornament joined only to the medallion, with nothing above or between them; a small pointed bronze foot. Shown perfectly upright, the winged head at the top.
fix.note: keep the V of wings round a medallion, the line's defining part; ours is dark bronze, plain leaf-shaped plates and a milky stone, not the original's bright gilt feathered wings; the narrow V keeps the outline off s404's 0.479. Paint it with invmsf's new words in the same run and pick the two together so the shafts match

invmsf.reason: At 1x the serpent is lost: a thin dark bronze snake on a dark bronze rod (1x median luminance ~47 on the #070605 grid) reads as a plain dark stick with a point, nothing of the serpent-wound shaft the quest item is known by; and its pair invhst goes back, so the two shafts should be painted and picked together to match.

fix.desc: The headless shaft of an ancient order of mages' staff: a straight rod of dark bronze with a thick carved serpent of worn brass coiling round it from foot to top in five open turns, the coils as thick as the rod and standing out from it with dark gaps between them, fine scales on the serpent, its head resting just under the top; the top end an open bronze socket, a short collar with an empty hole where a head-piece is missing; a small pointed bronze foot. Shown perfectly upright, the open socket at the top.
fix.note: the same shaft words as invhst's; a separate bold brass serpent round a dark rod (ours), not the original's shaft that is itself a gilt twist; s404 (0.23) is the fallback if the new words go wrong

fix.desc: A plain apprentice's wand: a straight rod of polished warm mid-brown hardwood as thick as a thumb, a little thicker toward the top, banded under its head by three broad rings of tarnished bronze; its head a bronze cup of three short claws holding a round dull amber stone about twice as wide as the rod; a grip wrapped in dark cord at the lower end and a small rounded bronze butt knob. A sturdy wand, lighter in tone than the yew and grim wands. Shown upright, the stone at the top.

invtri.reason: A hay fork, not a war trident: none of the four seeds has the barbed points the words ask for, and the three thin round tines on a bowed crossbar are a farm pitchfork's; at 1x the line's defining part (barbed prongs) is missing.

fix.desc: A trident, a three-pronged war fork: a long straight wooden shaft with an iron socket; at the top a short, straight, heavy iron crossbar carrying three thick, straight, square-sectioned iron prongs, the middle one a little longer, each ending in a flat arrow-shaped barbed head clearly wider than its prong, its two barbs pointing back down; a leather grip wrap below the socket and an iron butt cap. Thick forged iron, not a farm fork's thin round tines. Shown perfectly upright, the prongs at the top, front view.
